## PROJECT: WFX ERP — SALES ORDER MODULE TRANSFORMATION
### Enterprise-grade Apparel Sales Order Management

Act as a **Senior ERP Solution Architect, Business Analyst, Angular Architect, UI/UX Designer, Database Engineer and QA Engineer** working together to transform my existing WFX ERP application into a fully functional, enterprise-grade apparel Sales Order Management system.

This is not a request to create a basic Sales Order form or a static UI prototype.

I want you to understand the WFX apparel business processes, existing application architecture, existing modules, functional specifications, screenshots, transaction dependencies and business rules before implementing the Sales Order module.

Your responsibility is to understand the complete business process and then implement it properly.

Do not merely provide recommendations, diagrams, or a development plan. Analyse the project, make actual code changes, connect the functionality, test the workflows and deliver a working implementation.

---

## 1. FIRST: UNDERSTAND THE EXISTING PROJECT AND SOURCE MATERIAL

Before writing any code, perform a complete audit of the existing application.

#### Documents to study

Locate and read the following documents:

1. Sales Order Sprint 1
2. Sales Order Sprint 2
3. Sales Order Sprint 3 / Sales Order Sprint - 3 V2

Read the complete documents, including:
- Functional requirements.
- Business rules.
- Field descriptions.
- Transaction flows.
- Validation rules.
- Images and screenshots embedded inside DOCX files.
- UI references.
- Special cases and exceptions.
- Existing prototypes and screen designs.

Do not limit your analysis to extracting text from DOCX files. Inspect embedded screenshots and understand what the user is expected to do on each screen.

Search the entire project workspace for these documents. If any document is unavailable, explicitly record it as missing rather than assuming its requirements.

#### Existing project audit

Inspect the existing implementation of:

- Article Management
- BOM Management
- Routing Management
- Costing Management
- Sales Order, if partially implemented
- Buyer Master
- Style Master
- Company and Division configuration
- Existing permissions
- Shared data services and API integrations
- Database structure and relationships
- Common UI components and design system

These modules have already been created or are being developed in this project.

**Do not recreate them. Do not develop duplicate functionality.**

Understand their existing data structures and connect Sales Order with them wherever the documented business process requires.

Also inspect the existing Sales Order New page HTML prototypes if available. Use them as additional design and workflow references, not as an excuse to reuse hardcoded demonstration data or outdated business logic.

#### Create a requirement mapping before implementation

Prepare an internal requirement matrix containing:

| Area | Requirement | Source | Existing Module Dependency | Implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales Order List | Main OC Wise / Style Wise | Screenshot / Specs | Sales Order | Required |
| New Order | Category and Buyer | Screenshot | Buyer Master | Required |
| Buyer Configuration | Configurable fields | Sprint specifications | SLC | Required |
| Article | Multiple articles | Sprint 3 | Article | Required |
| BOM | Article-related BOM | Existing project / Specs | BOM | Integration |
| Costing | Selling price and cost integration | Sprint 2 / 3 | Costing | Integration |
| Routing | Existing routing association | Existing project | Routing | Integration |
| Deliveries | Delivery management | Sprint 2 / 3 | Sales Order | Required |
| Approval | Approval workflow | Sprint 2 | Permissions | Required |
| History | Transaction audit | Sprint 2 / 3 | Activity Timeline | Required |

Resolve dependencies from the actual code and source documentation.

If a requirement is unclear or two sources conflict, maintain a documented open-point list. Do not silently invent or change business rules.

---

## 2. UNDERSTAND THE BUSINESS PURPOSE

Sales Order is the buyer-facing order management process for apparel manufacturing.

The system must support the complete journey:

Buyer → Category → Sales Order / Main OC → Style → Delivery OC → Article → Color/Size → Quantities → Pricing → BOM / Costing / Routing association → Production and downstream transactions.

The application must understand the distinction between:

- Main OC (Main Order Confirmation).
- Delivery OC / DOC.
- Style.
- Article.
- Buyer.
- Buyer Order Reference.
- Order Quantity.
- ASN Quantity.
- GDN Quantity.

These are related but are not interchangeable entities.

Maintain the correct parent-child relationships between the main order, its deliveries, styles and articles.

Do not flatten everything into one generic Sales Order record.

The system must support apparel-specific requirements such as multiple styles, multiple articles, size matrices, color matrices, multiple deliveries, assorted packing and additional quantity management.

---

## 3. SALES ORDER NAVIGATION AND INITIAL LIST SCREEN

Navigation:

Sales → Sales Order List

Use the first supplied screenshot as the primary reference for the Sales Order List.

Retain the existing WFX ERP navigation shell and overall design language.

#### Default view: Main OC Wise

When the user opens Sales Order List, the default view should be:

Main OC Wise

This view displays Sales Order information at the Main OC level.

The user must also have an option to switch to:

Style Wise

#### Main OC Wise vs Style Wise

Main OC Wise:
- Show information organized around the Main OC.
- Display associated buyer, order information and delivery-related information.
- Allow users to drill into the relevant order and delivery details.

Style Wise:
- Show information organized around the styles associated with Sales Orders.
- Allow users to identify orders and deliveries associated with a particular style.
- Preserve the relationship with the parent Main OC.

Do not implement these as two unrelated data sources. They must be two presentation/grouping modes over the correct underlying Sales Order data.

#### List screen controls

Implement the controls shown in the reference:

1. Search by Order Number.
2. Main OC Wise / Style Wise selector.
3. Status filter.
4. Buyer filter.
5. Refresh.
6. Header context menu.
7. Filters panel.
8. Row-level checkbox selection.
9. Column-level filters.
10. Pagination and page-size selection.
11. Horizontal and vertical scrolling.
12. Row-level three-dot context menu.

#### Suggested visible columns

Follow the supplied screenshot and actual available data for columns such as:

- Article
- Status
- Buyer
- Order
- Order Quantity
- ASN Quantity
- GDN Quantity
- Season
- Buyer Order Date
- Buyer Delivery Date
- OC Delivery Date
- Progress

Use actual configured columns and field visibility rules.

The list must support thousands of records without rendering the complete dataset unnecessarily.

Implement suitable server-side pagination, filtering, debounced search and efficient data loading where supported by the existing architecture.

Do not hardcode sample record counts or placeholder order data.

---

## 4. ADD NEW SALES ORDER — INITIAL ENTRY FLOW

This is the first workflow to implement.

Navigation:

Sales → Sales Order List → Add New Order

Use my second screenshot as the exact reference for this initial popup.

When the user clicks **+ Add New Order**, open a centered modal.

#### Popup title

Add New Order

#### Fields

1. Category (Mandatory)
2. Buyer (Mandatory)

Both fields must use existing master data.

The Buyer field should follow the category dependency shown in the screenshot. Verify its actual dependency against the existing data and business rules rather than hardcoding values.

#### Popup actions

- Cancel
- OK
- Close icon

#### Expected behavior

1. User clicks Add New Order.
2. Popup opens.
3. User selects Category.
4. User selects Buyer.
5. User clicks OK.
6. System validates the selection.
7. System loads the appropriate buyer-specific Sales Order configuration.
8. User enters the actual Sales Order creation screen.

Category and Buyer selection should establish the context for the new order.

Do not expose every possible Sales Order field to every buyer.

This is one of the most important requirements of the entire module.

---

## 5. BUYER-WISE FIELD CONFIGURATION — CORE BUSINESS REQUIREMENT

In WFX, buyers may have different business processes.

Some buyers work with particular fields, while other buyers do not require them.

The system must therefore support buyer-specific field configuration.

For example:

Buyer A may need:
- Buyer Style Reference
- Season
- Buyer Order Reference
- Delivery Dates
- Shipment Mode

Buyer B may have a completely different set of configured fields.

These are illustrative examples, not fixed field configurations.

**The system must not display unnecessary fields to a buyer or force users to enter information that their buyer configuration does not require.**

#### Configuration mechanism

Inspect and implement the existing SLC / View Configurator functionality.

The documented navigation is:

Admin → Configurator → SLC → Sales Order → Setup (New, List)

Use the existing configurator wherever possible.

#### Configurable field properties

Support the documented configuration options:

- Field visibility.
- Field ordering.
- Mandatory status for New screen fields.
- Editable / Read Only status.
- Field type.
- Validation type.
- Single-select / Multi-select dropdown.

#### Additional Fields

As specified in Sprint 3, rename Flex Field to:

Additional Fields

The Add Field popup should support:

Field Types:
1. Alphanumeric
2. Dropdown
3. Date
4. Numeric Box
5. Text Box

Dropdown should support a single-select or multi-select option.

Validation Types:
1. None
2. Alphanumeric
3. Numeric

Users should be able to:
- Add a field.
- Configure the field.
- Drag it into Selected Fields.
- Arrange its position.
- Configure Mandatory and Editable properties where applicable.
- Save the configuration.

Important documented corrections:

- Mandatory and Edit fields are not required on the SLC List screen.
- Sales Order New page View Configurator must not have right-pin or left-pin tools.

#### Buyer-wise configuration resolution

After selecting a buyer:

1. Retrieve the appropriate buyer-specific configuration.
2. Identify the configured screen view.
3. Load the visible fields.
4. Apply Mandatory / Editable properties.
5. Apply field types and validations.
6. Preserve configured ordering.
7. Load the correct default values only where supported by existing business logic.

Do not create one global field configuration and apply it to every buyer.

If multiple saved views are available, provide the appropriate buyer-wise view selection using the existing View Configurator and permission mechanism.

---

## 6. SALES ORDER CREATION PAGE

After Category and Buyer are selected and the user clicks OK, open the Sales Order creation page.

Study the existing Sales Order New page prototype before finalizing the screen structure.

Maintain the existing WFX design language.

The page should be organized into meaningful sections rather than a huge unstructured form.

The existing prototype includes the following navigation concepts:

Retain and improve these where relevant to the documented flow.

#### Order Information

The information section should load fields based on the selected buyer's configuration.

#### Deliveries section

The Sales Order page must support multiple deliveries.

Use a dedicated left-side Deliveries panel.

## 7. DELIVERY MANAGEMENT

Implement the documented delivery-level operations.

#### Add Delivery

A new delivery can be created through:

1. Add Delivery button.

When creating a completely new delivery:

#### Copy Delivery

Allow users to copy an existing delivery.

The copied delivery should retain the applicable information from the source delivery while allowing the user to modify the newly created delivery.

Never overwrite the source delivery.

#### Delete Delivery

- Support single and multiple delivery selection.

#### Split Delivery

Support:

#### Reopen Delivery

- Support reopening eligible closed deliveries.
- Capture remarks.
- Confirm the action.
- Update the status.
- Make the delivery editable again according to permissions.

Maintain distinct status behavior for Main OC and Delivery OC. Do not mix these workflows.

## 9. BOM, ROUTING AND COSTING INTEGRATION

#### Article → BOM

#### Article / Style → Routing

Inspect the existing Routing module.

#### Costing integration

Connect the Sales Order with the existing Costing module.

Use Sprint 2's documented desync functionality.

Implement the documented Price Per levels:

3. Size.
4. Color/Size.

Final Selling Price = Base Selling Price ± Upcharge/Discount

- Lock the opposite input where required by the specification.

## 15. UI/UX EXPECTATIONS — WFX ERP STANDARD

The current screenshots are the primary reference for the Sales Order List and Add New Order popup.

I want the application to look like a professional WFX ERP enterprise product.

Do not create a generic SaaS dashboard.

#### Design principles

- Maintain WFX navigation and visual identity.
- Compact enterprise-style screens.
- Clean white and light-gray surfaces.
- Consistent WFX cyan/teal primary actions.
- Subtle borders and separators.
- Clear visual hierarchy.
- Consistent typography.
- Professional status indicators.
- Dense but readable tables.
- Properly aligned controls.
- Intuitive contextual actions.
- Sticky headers and columns where appropriate.
- Smooth and predictable scrolling.

#### Data-heavy screens

Sales Order is a highly data-intensive module.

Design it to support:
- Large article lists.
- Multiple deliveries.
- Color/Size matrices.
- Large order quantities.
- Multiple pricing levels.
- Wide data tables.

Avoid unnecessarily oversized cards and excessive empty space.

#### Responsive behavior

Support:
- Desktop.
- Laptop.
- Tablet.
- Mobile.

Do not simply shrink the desktop screen.

Adapt the layout intelligently while keeping every important action accessible.

On narrow screens, use responsive sections, compact layouts and controlled horizontal scrolling where necessary.

---

## 16. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION EXPECTATIONS

The project is expected to follow the existing Angular architecture. Verify the actual repository before making framework or architectural decisions.

#### Architecture

Use the existing:
- Routing structure.
- Services.
- Shared components.
- Design system.
- State-management pattern.
- Authentication.
- Permission system.
- API integrations.
- Database structure.

Do not rewrite unrelated modules.

#### Data integrity

Maintain proper relationships between:

Sales Order → Delivery → Style → Article → BOM / Costing / Routing references.

Use the existing master data.

Ensure correct foreign-key relationships, validation, persistence and transaction consistency.

Do not duplicate data unnecessarily.

#### Performance

Optimize:
- Large data grids.
- API requests.
- Filter operations.
- Search.
- Rendering.
- Color/Size matrices.
- Dynamic buyer configuration loading.

Use appropriate pagination, caching and lazy loading without compromising data correctness.

#### Functionality

Every button and menu item must perform its intended operation.

Every popup must have working validation and save/cancel behavior.

Every dropdown must retrieve the correct data.

Every page transition must navigate to the correct screen.

Every transaction must persist through the application's actual data layer.

Do not implement fake success messages, non-functional buttons or static demonstrations in place of real behavior.

If a backend dependency is missing, implement the correct integration boundary and document the limitation instead of pretending persistence has been completed.

---

## 17. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES

Execute the implementation in the following order.

#### Phase 0 — Application and Specification Audit
- Inspect the repository.
- Locate the sprint documents and all embedded images.
- Understand existing modules and database relationships.
- Identify missing dependencies.
- Create a requirement coverage matrix.

#### Phase 1 — Sales Order List
- Main OC Wise.
- Style Wise.
- Search.
- Filters.
- Grid behavior.
- Pagination.
- Row actions.
- Header actions.

#### Phase 2 — Add New Order
- Category and Buyer modal.
- Buyer-dependent configuration.
- SLC/View Configurator integration.
- Additional Fields.

#### Phase 3 — Sales Order Creation Page
- Order Information.
- Instruction.
- Documents.
- Deliveries sidebar.
- Add/Edit Delivery.
- Article Information.

#### Phase 4 — Cross-Module Integration
- Article.
- BOM.
- Routing.
- Costing.
- Price synchronization.
- Color/Size quantities.
- Packing and Additional Quantity.

#### Phase 5 — Transaction Workflows
- Approval.
- History.
- Delivery actions.
- Main OC actions.
- Tool permissions.
- ASN/GDN.
- Dispatch.
- TNA.
- Notes.
- MRP.
- Transfer Price.
- EDI Buyer PO.

#### Phase 6 — Testing and Refinement
- Functional testing.
- Business-rule validation.
- API testing.
- Permission testing.
- Data-integrity testing.
- Responsive testing.
- Performance testing.
- End-to-end workflow testing.

Do not stop after completing the initial popup or list screen.

Continue implementing the complete scope in these phases without waiting for approval after each phase.

---

## 18. MANDATORY END-TO-END TEST SCENARIO

Use this as the primary acceptance workflow.

1. Navigate to Sales → Sales Order List.
2. Verify Main OC Wise as the default view.
3. Switch to Style Wise and verify its behavior.
4. Click Add New Order.
5. Select Category = Apparel.
6. Select an available Buyer.
7. Click OK.
8. Verify buyer-specific field configuration.
9. Verify that only applicable fields are displayed.
10. Enter Sales Order Information.
11. Add a Delivery.
12. Add a Style.
13. Add the associated Article or Articles.
14. Retrieve the appropriate BOM association.
15. Verify the existing Routing association.
16. Retrieve the relevant Costing / Selling Price information.
17. Enter Color/Size combinations.
18. Enter order quantities.
19. Verify packing and additional quantity behavior.
20. Save the Delivery.
21. Add another Delivery and verify that the first remains unchanged.
22. Confirm the Sales Order.
23. Verify whether approval is required.
24. Complete the approval workflow where applicable.
25. Verify the resulting order status.
26. Return to Sales Order List.
27. Verify the order in Main OC Wise and Style Wise.
28. Open the order and verify delivery and article details.
29. Verify that all activities appear in History.

Also test each individual action against its documented business rules.

---

## 19. DEFINITION OF DONE

The Sales Order module will be considered complete only when:

- The list screen works.
- Main OC Wise and Style Wise work independently and correctly.
- The Category/Buyer popup works.
- Buyer-specific field configuration works.
- The order creation page works.
- Multiple deliveries work.
- Article integration works.
- BOM integration works.
- Routing integration follows the existing model.
- Costing and price integration work.
- Color/Size quantity handling works.
- Packing and additional quantity rules work.
- Approval processes work.
- Delivery and Main OC actions work.
- Permissions are enforced.
- History and Activity Timeline are reliable.
- All important actions are functional.
- Data persists correctly.
- The screens work on different device sizes.
- No existing project functionality is broken.

All implemented features must have corresponding test coverage.

---

## 20. FINAL INSTRUCTIONS — DO NOT IGNORE

I want you to approach this as an actual ERP product implementation, not a UI assignment.

The earlier implementation attempts in this project have suffered from:
- Generic UI.
- Poor workflow understanding.
- Repetitive diagrams.
- Hardcoded information.
- Non-functional buttons.
- Disconnected modules.
- Missing data relationships.

Do not repeat these mistakes.

Before implementing a screen, understand why that screen exists in the business process.

Before implementing a field, understand which buyer or transaction needs it.

Before connecting a module, understand its existing data relationship.

Before implementing a transaction, understand its effect on the Main OC, Delivery OC, Style and Article.

**The most important principle: BUILD THE BUSINESS PROCESS, NOT JUST THE SCREENS.**

Make actual code changes. Reuse the existing application architecture. Implement the functionality end to end. Run builds and tests, fix errors and verify the workflows.

At completion, provide:
1. Modules and components changed.
2. Functionalities implemented.
3. Existing modules successfully integrated.
4. Database/API changes.
5. Tests executed and results.
6. Remaining requirements and genuine blockers.
7. Any unresolved business-rule questions.

Do not claim a feature is complete unless it has actually been implemented and verified.

#### Claude · 2026-11-19 09:21

Both parts are done and live at http://192.168.100.196:8787/. All 144 tests pass.

**1. Workflows no longer assume Buyer Block Booking**

What was wrong:
- Opening **Workflows** with nothing selected silently loaded the Buyer Block Booking chain.
- **Sales Order to factory** always included "Link Buyer Block Booking" and "Automatic adjustment".
- The Sales Order and Planning modules' Workflow shortcuts added booking steps too.

What it does now:
- **Workflows opens empty** ("0 of 32 selected"). The user ticks the steps their process needs, or picks a ready-made workflow and changes it.
- **Sales Order to factory has 8 steps and no booking:** Create Sales Order → MRP → Manufacture Indent → Sales Order Indent → PO for what's still to buy → Production Order → FPO → Process orders. The booking simulator appears only when the user adds booking steps.
- **Block Booking is one option among the ready-made workflows**, no longer the first one, and its description says it applies only when the buyer books ahead.
- **Module shortcuts open only their own steps.** Booking steps belong to the Booking & sourcing module.
- **The workflow designer on the server already treated booking as an optional branch**, so it's unchanged.

A test now fails if a booking step creeps back into a non-booking workflow or module.

**2. Training the bot with an LLM**

An LLM can't simply learn your knowledge without risking invented answers. So the setup keeps answers as your source text and uses the LLM where it's safe: writing the many ways users ask a question.

- **Export:** `npm run kb:export-training` writes five files to `exports/llm-training/`:
  - all 661 approved/active knowledge entries, each with its source, for an LLM's search index;
  - 684 training and 84 validation question-and-answer pairs in the standard chat format, with validation kept to topics not seen in training;
  - 130 held-out test questions, never used for training (I found and fixed a leak where two had slipped in);
  - one prompt per knowledge unit (95) asking an LLM for more user-style questions, with strict rules: only what the text says, no new facts.
- **Import:** `npm run kb:import-questions -- replies.jsonl --model "<name>"` brings the LLM's questions back.
  - They're checked: the unit must exist, they must be plain questions, and duplicates are skipped.
  - They arrive as **unreviewed proposals** on Knowledge › Question mapping, where you approve or reject them.
  - The answer always stays your source's own text.
- **Measure:** after each round, `npm run kb:eval-paraphrase -- --test` shows whether the questions you've approved actually help.

#### Claude · 2026-11-19 10:15

Claude in Atlas can now write the training questions for you, from **Knowledge › Question mapping**. It's built, tested and live, but it stays switched off until you add your API key and record the approval.

**How it works**
- **Claude: write questions** on a module's row (e.g. Sales Order): Claude writes questions for up to 10 knowledge units that don't have any from Claude yet. Click again for the next 10.
- **Ask Claude for more questions** inside a unit: Claude writes questions for that one unit.
- **What Claude gets:** the unit's own source text plus strict rules. Every question must be answerable from that text alone, with no new facts or screens, 8–20 varied questions (informal, short, problem-oriented, abbreviations, typos) and no repeats of existing ones.
- **What happens to its questions:** they go through the same checks as a file import and arrive as **unreviewed proposals**. The new filter **Claude proposals to review** lists the units waiting for you to approve, edit or reject. The answers never change: they stay your source text.
- **After each run** you see how many questions were added, were already there, were refused by the checks or failed, and how many tokens it used.
- **To measure the effect** after reviewing, run:

```powershell
npm run kb:eval-paraphrase -- --test
```

I tested it with a stand-in for Claude: a good reply, an unreadable reply and a refusal. Only the valid new question was stored, as an unreviewed proposal on the unit that was asked. All 145 tests pass, and it's committed and deployed.

1. Open `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\.env` and set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` to your key. Type it there yourself; don't paste it into this chat.
2. Restart the server in [WFX server D](#terminal/c13).
3. Sign in as admin and record the approval in **Admin › AI provider**.

#### Claude · 2026-11-16 05:40

Phase 7, the data modelling studio, is built and works. You open it from the new **Data Modelling** tab (`/data-modelling`). All 74 platform tests pass, and the site build passes. I also clicked through it in the browser on the throw-away sandbox copy; nothing was saved to your real knowledge base.

**What it does:**
- **Captured WFX models:** opens any of the 28 recorded document models, or a map of all of them, as an ER diagram. A field that takes its value from another document becomes a link marked documented, for example GRN lines to RMPO 1229. That a grid holds its document's lines is marked inferred, because no source says so.
- **Drafts from a requirement:** you write statements like "Supplier: code (key), name" or "An order has many lines". It understands one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many. Any sentence it doesn't understand is listed as not understood, never guessed.
- **Logical view:** adds the missing keys, the links between tables, and an extra table for each many-to-many. Everything it adds is marked inferred.
- **Checks:** missing keys, repeated or multi-value fields, fields copied from another document, derived (calculated) fields, links to entities that don't exist, and duplicated attributes.
- **Outputs:** a data dictionary, a Mermaid ER diagram, and an SQL draft whose first line says it is a proposal and not the WFX database schema. For captured models it writes no table-to-table links, because WFX's key columns aren't documented.
- **Editing and saving:** you can drag, arrange and edit entities, attributes and relationships, then save as a versioned Draft. It is approved through the Rulebook like any other entry.

**Safeguards:**
- A draft can never overwrite a captured model.
- The assistant's data-model answers only use captured, Approved or Active models, so a draft is never quoted as confirmed WFX knowledge.

**Fixed during the browser check:** the relationship labels were hidden behind the entity boxes. They are now drawn on top, with more space between columns.

**Still limited:**
- The actual WFX database tables and keys can't be modelled until real database metadata is available.
- It only understands the sentence patterns listed above. Freer writing would need the AI provider, once your organisation approves it.

The main code is in `backend/src/datamodel/studio.ts` and `src/app/platform/data-modelling.ts`. The roadmap, implementation log, testing report, architecture, changelog and README are updated.

#### Claude · 2026-11-16 09:46

The token you typed, `724776`, isn't the setup token. The real one is a long random string of about 24 letters and digits, so it's easy to tell apart. Your password is also too short, and that will be the next error.

**1. Copy the real token.** Open the Terminal tab [WFX server D](#terminal/c1). Under the line "FIRST START: … create the admin account with this one-time setup token" there is a blank line and then the token. Select that line and copy it with Ctrl+C. Copy and paste instead of typing, since the characters are easy to mix up.

**2. Fill the form again.**
- **Setup token:** paste it, with no spaces before or after.
- **User name:** `Still_Unknown` is fine.
- **Password:** at least 10 characters, mixing letters with digits or symbols. Yours shows 6 dots, so the page would refuse it. Something like a phrase plus a number and a symbol works.
- **Repeat password:** type the same again.

**3. If it still says the token is not valid.** A new token is made each time the server starts, and the old one stops working. If the server was restarted since you copied it, copy the latest token from that tab. A fresh token only appears at a start while no admin exists yet. If you can't find it, stop the server in that tab with Ctrl+C and run `npm run kb:server` again in `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN`. That prints a new token.

#### Claude · 2026-11-17 03:35

You can now create your own account from the sign-in page. Your `D:` server runs the new code, and I tested the whole flow in the browser on the sandbox copy.

**How it works**
- **Create an account:** the sign-in page has this link, and the form takes your name, a user name and a password twice. It shows the password rules and says what will happen next.
- **Always a viewer:** a self-made account can read and ask, nothing more. It cannot change knowledge, even in open mode.
- **Default needs approval:** the account waits, and it cannot sign in until an admin approves it.
- **Approving in Admin:** the request shows as "waiting for approval". The admin picks a role (viewer, editor, approver or admin) and clicks **Approve**, or clicks **Reject** to delete the request.
- **Admin setting:** Admin → Users and roles has a selector with three choices:
  - off: only an admin adds users
  - approval: the default
  - open: the account is active at once, so anybody who can reach the server reads the WFX knowledge, and I'd only use that on a private network.

**Safeguards**
- Five account requests per hour per computer, and at most 50 pending at a time.
- A wrong password never reveals that an account is pending; the "waiting" message appears only when the password is right.
- Sign-up is refused until the first admin exists.
- Every sign-up, approval, rejection and mode change goes into the audit trail.
- There is no email check, because there is no mail service, so admin approval is the control.

**You still need an admin account.** An account made from the page starts as a viewer waiting for approval, and nobody can approve it unless an admin can sign in. You said you couldn't sign in, so use the Terminal tab [Create my admin](#terminal/c6) once. It's started and waiting for **you** to type the password, hidden, twice. Then sign in as `Nishant724776`, and from then on use Admin for everything else. You now have a **Profile** page where admins can add new users, and the user list is stored in an admin text file. I did not build a vector database. Your `D:` server is restarted with all of this, and the file already exists with your two accounts.

**Profile page**
- **Where to find it:** open **Knowledge → Profile**, or click your name at the top right. The address is `http://127.0.0.1:8787/profile`.
- **Every user sees:** their name, user name, role, when the account was created and the last sign-in, plus a form to change their password.
- **Admins also see an "Add a new user" form:** name, user name, role (viewer, editor, approver or admin) and a first password.
- **After adding:** the new user can sign in at once with that password, and they can change it on their own Profile page.
- **Same tools as before:** **Admin** still has the full user list, approvals and the sign-up setting.

**Admin text file**
- **What it is:** `knowledge/admin/users.txt` lists each account with its name, role, status and creation date. In your copy that is `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\knowledge\admin\users.txt`.
- **When it updates:** it is rewritten whenever an account is added, approved, rejected, disabled or its role changes, and again when the server starts.
- **No passwords, ever:** it holds no passwords, password hashes or tokens. Passwords stay only in the database, scrambled.
- **Edits to the file do nothing:** it is regenerated, so use Profile or Admin to change accounts.

**Searching it (RAG)**
- **Who can search it:** the same text is added to the search index, but only for administrators. An admin can ask the assistant "which user has the approver role?" and get an answer citing the directory.
- **Nobody else:** viewers, editors and approvers can never retrieve it, and a test proves that.
- **New names:** a name added since the last re-index may not be understood by name yet, so ask by role, or use Admin → Re-index.

**Vector database: not built.** Search here is full-text, with synonyms and ranking. A real vector database needs an embedding model, which means an AI key and your organisation's approval to send text to it. I didn't want to label plain keyword search as vector search. If you get that approval, I can add real vector search.

### Designer problems I found and fixed
- **Tangled flowchart.** The 35-step flow was a mess of long lines behind boxes. It now arranges itself in layers with fewer crossings.

#### Claude · 2026-11-18 06:53

The link for anyone on the same Wi-Fi is:

**http://192.168.100.196:8787/**

I restarted your D: server so it listens on the network, and the address responds from this computer. I haven't tried it from a second computer.

**Things to know:**
- **Your computer must stay on**, with the server tab running. If your computer's IP address changes (for example after reconnecting to Wi-Fi), the link changes too.
- **Windows may ask to allow Node.js through the firewall.** Choose "Private networks". If another person can't open the link, this is the usual cause.
- **Each person needs an account.** They use "Create an account" on the sign-in page. You approve them under Admin, because sign-up currently needs your approval.
- **The connection is plain HTTP.** That is fine on a trusted office network, but don't share the link outside it.
- **To start it this way next time**, run `start-on-network.ps1` in the D: folder. It prints the current link and starts the server. A normal `npm run kb:server` listens only on your own computer.

## MASTER IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT: Intelligent AI Chatbot + WFX ERP Knowledge Assistant + Visual Workflow Navigation

### Project Objective

I want to transform the chatbot in my existing Angular application into an intelligent, context-aware AI assistant that understands WFX ERP, its modules, business processes, workflows, screens, transaction rules, and application navigation.

The chatbot should not behave like a basic question-answering application.

It should work as an intelligent ERP product assistant that helps users understand business functionality, learn how a process works, see visual demonstrations, and directly navigate to the relevant screen to perform an operation.

**Core objective: Don't make users read lengthy documentation or manually search through the application. Help them understand and perform tasks through visual explanations and direct navigation.**

The implementation must include:
- Real AI model integration through backend APIs.
- Database-backed conversation management.
- WFX ERP knowledge base.
- Workflow understanding and intelligent search.
- Screenshot-based, step-by-step visual guidance.
- Direct navigation to relevant ERP screens and workflows.
- Interactive and responsive chatbot UI.
- Actual working functionality, not a static prototype.

---

## 1. First Analyse the Existing Application

Before implementing anything, thoroughly inspect the existing project.

Understand:
- Existing Angular version and architecture.
- Existing backend and API structure.
- Existing database and data models.
- Existing routing and navigation mechanisms.
- Existing authentication and user permissions.
- Existing ERP modules and screens.
- Existing workflow diagrams, documentation, SRS, FRD, BRD and transaction rules.
- Existing design system and reusable components.

Reuse the existing application architecture wherever possible.

Do not create duplicate databases, API services, routing mechanisms, or components.

Do not remove or modify existing functionality unnecessarily.

The chatbot must integrate naturally into the existing application.

## 2. AI Chatbot: Ask Anything

Create a fully functional AI chatbot that allows users to ask questions using natural language.

Users should be able to ask questions such as:

- What is a Sales Order?
- Explain the complete Sales Order workflow.
- How does the GRN process work?
- How do I create a Purchase Order?
- What is the difference between GRN and GDN?
- How does Material Requirement Planning work?
- Where can I configure workflow settings?
- How do I generate a Shipping Bill?
- Explain the Trims Scan process.
- How can I execute the outward process?

The chatbot must understand the intent behind questions, even when users use informal language, incomplete sentences, abbreviations, or different terminology for the same functionality.

It should also support general questions unrelated to WFX ERP.

The chatbot must:
- Maintain conversational context.
- Understand follow-up questions.
- Generate intelligent and relevant responses.
- Remember the current conversation context.
- Ask a clarification question when the requested functionality is ambiguous.
- Avoid generating irrelevant or generic responses.

## 3. WFX ERP Knowledge Base and Intelligence

This is one of the most important requirements.

The chatbot must understand actual WFX ERP product knowledge rather than guessing how the application works.

Build an organised knowledge base using available project documentation and application information.

The knowledge base should support:

**A. ERP modules**
- Sales
- Purchase
- Sourcing
- Inventory
- Production
- Shipping
- Finance
- Quality
- Configuration
- Reports
- Other modules available in the actual project.

**B. Business processes**

Store information about:
- Process definitions.
- Business objectives.
- Prerequisites.
- Transaction sequences.
- Business rules.
- Dependencies.
- Validation rules.
- Required permissions.
- Input and output.
- Expected transaction results.
- Exception scenarios.

**C. Application screens**

For every relevant screen, maintain:
- Screen name.
- Module name.
- Navigation path.
- Screen URL or Angular route.
- Purpose of the screen.
- Available actions.
- Field descriptions.
- Related workflows.
- Required permissions.

**D. Workflow information**

Maintain complete workflow knowledge, including:
- Workflow name.
- Workflow description.
- Workflow diagram.
- Starting point.
- Sequential steps.
- Decision points.
- Conditional paths.
- Alternate scenarios.
- Final outcome.
- Related screens.
- Direct navigation links.

Use a structured, searchable knowledge base. Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) where appropriate so the AI retrieves relevant WFX documentation and application knowledge before generating answers.

Do not rely solely on the LLM's general knowledge for WFX-specific business rules.

The chatbot must prioritise verified project information over assumptions.

When information is unavailable, it must clearly communicate that rather than inventing an ERP process.

## 4. Visual Step-by-Step Guidance with Actual Screenshots

This is a critical feature.

Users generally do not want to read lengthy explanations. They prefer to see what they need to do, where they need to click, and what result they should expect.

Therefore, the chatbot must provide visual, screenshot-based explanations whenever a user asks how to perform an operation.

### Example: User asks "How do I process a GRN?"

Instead of providing only a lengthy text response, the chatbot should display a visual walkthrough.

Example response structure:

**GRN Processing Guide**

Brief explanation of what GRN is and why it is required.

Then display the following steps:

**Step 1: Navigate to GRN**

- Show an actual screenshot of the relevant application screen.
- Highlight the exact menu or button to click.
- Add a numbered marker or visual pointer.
- Explain what the user needs to do.
- Explain what happens after clicking.

**Step 2: Select the Purchase Order**

- Show the next screenshot.
- Highlight the relevant selection field.
- Explain how the user should select the Purchase Order.
- Show the expected screen/result.

**Step 3: Enter GRN Details**

- Display the relevant screen.
- Highlight required fields.
- Explain the required values and validation rules.

**Step 4: Save and Confirm**

- Show the save/submit action.
- Explain the expected system response.
- Display the resulting GRN status or confirmation.

Continue until the complete business process is explained.

### Visual Presentation Requirements

Every visual step should ideally contain:

1. Step number and step title.
2. Actual application screenshot.
3. Highlighted click location.
4. Directional arrows, numbered pointers or visual annotations.
5. Short explanation.
6. Expected result.
7. Next-step navigation.

Users should be able to navigate through the walkthrough using Previous and Next controls.

Include a progress indicator such as Step 2 of 5.

Allow users to open an enlarged screenshot.

Use concise explanations rather than large paragraphs.

**Important:** Screenshots must represent the actual application UI, not invented or generic ERP screenshots.

Use available application screenshots, documented screen assets, browser screenshots, or screenshots captured from the running application.

## 5. Running Prototype Integration: Trims Scan

Use the following running prototype as a reference for understanding and demonstrating the Trims Scan process:

Prototype URL:
https://trims-prototype-mobile.vercel.app/

Prototype name: Trims Scan Prototype.

This is a clickable prototype showing trims handling through QR scanning in the Quick Docs mobile app.

It includes:
- GRN
- Pick List
- GDN
- Location
- Print Doc
- Outward Note

It currently uses sample data.

### Required Implementation

Inspect the running prototype and understand its complete interaction flow.

Capture actual screenshots of the important screens and steps wherever browser access or screenshot capture is available.

Create a visual walkthrough explaining:

- How the trims scanning process starts.
- How QR scanning works.
- How the user navigates through each transaction.
- What information is displayed at each stage.
- What action the user must perform.
- What result is expected after each action.
- How the process moves to the next stage.
- How the complete process is finished.

The chatbot should be able to answer questions such as:

- Explain the Trims Scan process.
- How do I scan trims against a GRN?
- How does Pick List scanning work?
- How do I generate a GDN?
- How do I handle location scanning?
- How do I print the document?
- Explain the complete outward process.

For these questions, display relevant screenshots with numbered step-by-step instructions.

Provide a clickable link to open the running prototype directly.

Do not mistake the prototype's sample data for live production transactions. Clearly distinguish prototype demonstrations from actual ERP functionality.

## 6. Intelligent Workflow Discovery and Direct Navigation

This is another major requirement.

The chatbot should understand which workflow, module, or specific application screen the user is searching for.

It should not just explain what a workflow is. It should also help the user access and execute it.

### Example 1: User searches "Sales Order Workflow"

The chatbot should identify the intent as a Sales Order workflow query.

It should display:

**Sales Order Workflow**

A brief explanation of the Sales Order process.

Then provide:

1. What is a Sales Order?
2. Why is it required?
3. What are the prerequisites?
4. How does the complete process work?
5. What are the important transaction rules?
6. What are the different stages?
7. What happens after completing each stage?

It should also display the actual Sales Order workflow diagram.

Below the explanation, provide relevant navigation actions:

- View Sales Order Workflow
- Open Sales Order Screen
- View Step-by-Step Guide

Each action must open the correct application page or workflow.

### Example 2: User asks "I want to create a Sales Order"

The chatbot should understand that the user wants to perform an operation, not merely learn about the concept.

Its response should contain:

- A brief explanation of the operation.
- Required prerequisites.
- A visual step-by-step guide with actual screenshots.
- Important validations and transaction rules.
- A direct action such as **Open Sales Order Creation**.

When the user clicks the action, the application should navigate directly to the actual Sales Order creation page.

The user should not have to search through the menus again.

### Example 3: User asks "Where can I configure workflow?"

The chatbot should identify the relevant configuration module.

Its response should explain:
- What the configuration is used for.
- How it affects the business process.
- Where it is configured.
- Which settings and permissions are required.

Then provide a direct link to the actual configuration page, subject to the user's permissions.

### Direct Navigation Requirements

Implement a central Screen and Workflow Registry.

Maintain structured mappings such as:

- Workflow ID.
- Workflow name.
- Module name.
- Screen name.
- Application route.
- Related documentation.
- Workflow diagram location.
- Screenshot references.
- Required permission.
- Navigation metadata.

The chatbot must retrieve actual routes from this registry.

When a user clicks a chatbot navigation link:

1. Validate that the destination is registered.
2. Check whether the user is authenticated.
3. Check whether the user has access to the destination.
4. Navigate directly to the relevant Angular route.
5. Preserve the appropriate application state where necessary.
6. Open the exact intended screen, not just the module landing page.

Use Angular Router or the existing navigation architecture.

Do not generate arbitrary routes using AI-generated strings.

For external HTML pages or prototypes, support registered, verified external URLs as well.

When direct access is not permitted, explain the permission restriction instead of bypassing it.

**The chatbot must work as an intelligent navigation assistant that takes users directly to the functionality they are looking for.**

## 7. Intelligent Query Classification

Implement an intent-classification and retrieval mechanism.

The chatbot should distinguish between:

| User intent | Expected chatbot behaviour |
|---|---|
| General question | Provide a conversational answer |
| ERP concept | Explain the concept using WFX knowledge |
| Workflow search | Show workflow diagram and explanation |
| How-to query | Show screenshot-based step-by-step guide |
| Screen search | Show direct application navigation link |
| Transaction execution | Explain prerequisites and guide the user to the relevant screen |
| Prototype search | Show prototype link and visual demonstration |
| Follow-up query | Continue using previous conversation context |

For example, when the user types "Sales Order", do not immediately return a generic definition.

Identify whether they are looking for:
- Sales Order concept.
- Sales Order workflow.
- Sales Order creation.
- Sales Order modification.
- Sales Order listing.
- Sales Order reports.

Present relevant options or ask a short clarification question when necessary.

## 8. Workflow Diagrams and Visual Explanations

Workflow visualisation must be a first-class feature.

Do not return basic, repetitive or generic flowcharts.

For every available workflow, display the actual business process with:

- Start and end nodes.
- Process steps.
- Decision nodes.
- Conditional branches.
- Alternate paths.
- Approval stages.
- Validation points.
- Connections and directional arrows.
- Clearly labelled transitions.

The diagram must reflect actual WFX business rules.

Provide a readable and interactive workflow visualisation.

Users should be able to zoom, pan, and select individual steps.

When a user selects a step, show its explanation, relevant screenshot, business rules, and related screen navigation.

The workflow diagram and the textual explanation must remain synchronised.

## 9. Chatbot Database and API Architecture

Develop actual backend APIs and database integration.

First inspect the existing backend and database and reuse them.

Create the required data models.

#### ChatConversation
- id
- userId
- title
- createdAt
- updatedAt

#### ChatMessage
- id
- conversationId
- role
- content
- status
- createdAt
- tokenUsage

#### ERPKnowledge
- id
- title
- module
- category
- content
- keywords
- relatedScreenIds
- relatedWorkflowIds
- sourceReference
- updatedAt

#### ERPWorkflow
- id
- workflowName
- module
- description
- workflowDefinition
- diagramReference
- relatedScreenIds
- prerequisites
- businessRules
- updatedAt

#### ERPScreenRegistry
- id
- screenName
- module
- applicationRoute
- description
- screenshotReferences
- requiredPermissions
- relatedWorkflowIds

#### VisualGuide
- id
- title
- relatedScreenId
- relatedWorkflowId
- steps
- screenshotReference
- annotations
- expectedResults

Adapt these entities to the existing database technology and naming conventions.

Do not introduce unnecessary duplicate records.

Support proper indexes, relationships, access control and migrations.

### Backend APIs

Implement endpoints equivalent to:

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/chat/conversations | Create conversation |
| GET | /api/chat/conversations | Get chat history |
| GET | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Get conversation |
| POST | /api/chat/conversations/:id/messages | Send message |
| PATCH | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Rename conversation |
| DELETE | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Delete conversation |
| POST | /api/chat/search | Search ERP knowledge |
| GET | /api/chat/workflows/:id | Retrieve workflow |
| GET | /api/chat/screens/:id | Retrieve screen information |
| GET | /api/chat/guides/:id | Retrieve visual walkthrough |
| GET | /api/chat/navigation/:id | Resolve registered navigation destination |

Implement proper validation, authentication, error handling and response structures.

## 10. AI Model and Knowledge Retrieval

Integrate an actual AI model through the backend.

Reuse any existing AI provider in the project. Otherwise, implement a provider-independent service layer using an official LLM API.

API keys must remain in backend environment variables.

The response-generation pipeline should work as follows:

1. Receive the user's question.
2. Identify the user's intent.
3. Retrieve relevant ERP knowledge.
4. Retrieve related workflow information.
5. Retrieve related screens and routes.
6. Retrieve screenshots and visual guides where applicable.
7. Check user permissions for navigation actions.
8. Generate a context-aware response.
9. Return the answer with structured visual content and relevant action links.
10. Store the conversation and response in the database.

Use structured AI responses so the frontend can distinguish between ordinary text, workflow diagrams, screenshots, step-by-step guides, and navigation actions.

Do not rely on free-form AI text alone to generate navigation links.

The application must be able to render these response types as appropriate.

## 11. Chatbot UI/UX Requirements

Design a modern, premium AI assistant interface consistent with the existing application.

Include:

- Chat history sidebar.
- New conversation button.
- Search previous conversations.
- Main conversation area.
- Suggested questions.
- Message input.
- Typing indicator.
- Stop generation.
- Copy response.
- Regenerate response.
- Relevant workflow cards.
- Screenshot-based guide cards.
- Direct navigation actions.
- Expandable workflow diagrams.
- Responsive mobile layout.

Responses should be visually structured.

For a complex operation, prefer a visual walkthrough with screenshots over several long paragraphs.

Keep the most relevant actions visible and easy to access.

The chatbot should feel like a knowledgeable product expert, not a generic customer support chatbot.

## 12. Testing Scenarios and Acceptance Criteria

Test the complete implementation with real API calls and actual stored data.

**Scenario A: General question**

User: "Explain APIs."

Expected: An intelligent response with examples.

**Scenario B: Workflow query**

User: "Show me the Sales Order workflow."

Expected:
- Relevant explanation.
- Actual workflow diagram.
- Step descriptions.
- Related screens.
- Direct workflow navigation.

**Scenario C: Operational query**

User: "How do I create a Sales Order?"

Expected:
- Prerequisites.
- Actual screenshots.
- Numbered click instructions.
- Expected results at each step.
- Direct Open Sales Order action.

**Scenario D: Trims Scan query**

User: "Explain the complete trims outward process."

Expected:
- Reference to the running Trims Scan prototype.
- Relevant screenshots.
- GRN, Pick List, GDN, Location, Print Doc and Outward Note steps.
- Actual step-by-step explanations.
- Direct prototype link.

**Scenario E: Direct screen navigation**

User: "Open the Sales Order screen."

Expected:
- Resolve the correct registered route.
- Check permissions.
- Navigate directly to the Sales Order screen.
- Do not redirect to the home page or module landing page.

**Scenario F: Unknown information**

User asks about a workflow that does not exist in the knowledge base.

Expected:
- Clearly state that verified information is unavailable.
- Do not invent business rules, routes, screenshots, or workflow steps.

**Scenario G: Persistence**

- Create a conversation.
- Ask multiple questions.
- Refresh the application.
- Reopen the conversation.
- Verify that the entire history is restored.

Also test mobile responsiveness, API failures, authorization, performance and existing application functionality.

## 13. Mandatory Implementation Rules

- Do not deliver just a chatbot UI.
- Do not deliver only architecture or code snippets.
- Do not use static responses as actual AI functionality.
- Do not use fake screenshots.
- Do not generate imaginary WFX business rules.
- Do not generate unregistered navigation links.
- Do not leave backend APIs as placeholders.
- Do not simulate database persistence using static arrays.
- Do not hardcode API credentials.
- Do not bypass permissions.
- Do not break existing application functionality.
- Do not make all chatbot responses lengthy text.
- Prioritise visual explanations and meaningful actions.
- Reuse existing components and architecture.
- Test each feature before marking it complete.

If screenshots, documentation, API credentials, routes or other required information are missing, identify the dependency clearly and implement everything that can be completed without inventing information.

## 14. Final Deliverables

After implementation, provide:

1. Working AI chatbot.
2. Backend APIs and their documentation.
3. Database schema and migrations.
4. AI provider integration.
5. WFX ERP knowledge-base implementation.
6. Intent classification and retrieval mechanism.
7. Screen and workflow registry.
8. Screenshot-based visual guidance system.
9. Workflow diagrams and interactive explanations.
10. Direct application navigation integration.
11. Responsive UI implementation.
12. Test results and known limitations.
13. Environment configuration and deployment instructions.

## FINAL PRODUCT VISION

I want users to interact with the application naturally.

They should be able to type:

"How does the Sales Order process work?"

The chatbot should understand the question, explain the business process, display an actual workflow diagram, show each step visually with screenshots, explain what the user needs to click, show the expected result, and provide a direct link to the Sales Order screen.

Similarly, when a user asks:

"How do I process trims outward?"

The chatbot should display the complete Trims Scan process with actual prototype screenshots, clear visual directions, and a link to open the prototype.

The user should never have to manually search through multiple menus, browse lengthy documentation, or guess which screen to open.

**Think of this as an AI-powered WFX ERP Product Expert + Process Trainer + Workflow Navigator combined into one intelligent assistant.**

The ultimate goal is to make the ERP application easier to learn, easier to navigate, and easier to operate — even for a completely new user.

Build this as a production-oriented, fully functional application feature, not a visual demonstration.

My additional recommendation
There are three important capabilities that will make this implementation significantly stronger:










1. Interactive visual tutorials

Instead of just showing screenshots, highlight the exact buttons and fields with numbered markers, arrows and explanations.

The chatbot should understand the relationship between business rules, workflow steps, screens, permissions and transactions.

Brief explanation of what GRN is and why it is required.

Then display the following steps:

**Step 1: Navigate to GRN**

- Show an actual screenshot of the relevant application screen.
- Highlight the exact menu or button to click.
- Add a numbered marker or visual pointer.
- Explain what the user needs to do.
- Explain what happens after clicking.

**Step 2: Select the Purchase Order**

- Show the next screenshot.
- Highlight the relevant selection field.
- Explain how the user should select the Purchase Order.
- Show the expected screen/result.

**Step 3: Enter GRN Details**

- Display the relevant screen.
- Highlight required fields.
- Explain the required values and validation rules.

**Step 4: Save and Confirm**

- Show the save/submit action.
- Explain the expected system response.
- Display the resulting GRN status or confirmation.

Continue until the complete business process is explained.

### Visual Presentation Requirements

Every visual step should ideally contain:

1. Step number and step title.
2. Actual application screenshot.
3. Highlighted click location.
4. Directional arrows, numbered pointers or visual annotations.
5. Short explanation.
6. Expected result.
7. Next-step navigation.

Users should be able to navigate through the walkthrough using Previous and Next controls.

Include a progress indicator such as Step 2 of 5.

Allow users to open an enlarged screenshot.

Use concise explanations rather than large paragraphs.

**Important:** Screenshots must represent the actual application UI, not invented or generic ERP screenshots.

Use available application screenshots, documented screen assets, browser screenshots, or screenshots captured from the running application.

## 5. Running Prototype Integration: Trims Scan

Use the following running prototype as a reference for understanding and demonstrating the Trims Scan process:

Prototype URL:
https://trims-prototype-mobile.vercel.app/

Prototype name: Trims Scan Prototype.

This is a clickable prototype showing trims handling through QR scanning in the Quick Docs mobile app.

It includes:
- GRN
- Pick List
- GDN
- Location
- Print Doc
- Outward Note

It currently uses sample data.

### Required Implementation

Inspect the running prototype and understand its complete interaction flow.

Capture actual screenshots of the important screens and steps wherever browser access or screenshot capture is available.

Create a visual walkthrough explaining:

- How the trims scanning process starts.
- How QR scanning works.
- How the user navigates through each transaction.
- What information is displayed at each stage.
- What action the user must perform.
- What result is expected after each action.
- How the process moves to the next stage.
- How the complete process is finished.

The chatbot should be able to answer questions such as:

- Explain the Trims Scan process.
- How do I scan trims against a GRN?
- How does Pick List scanning work?
- How do I generate a GDN?
- How do I handle location scanning?
- How do I print the document?
- Explain the complete outward process.

For these questions, display relevant screenshots with numbered step-by-step instructions.

Provide a clickable link to open the running prototype directly.

Do not mistake the prototype's sample data for live production transactions. Clearly distinguish prototype demonstrations from actual ERP functionality.

## 6. Intelligent Workflow Discovery and Direct Navigation

This is another major requirement.

The chatbot should understand which workflow, module, or specific application screen the user is searching for.

It should not just explain what a workflow is. It should also help the user access and execute it.

### Example 1: User searches "Sales Order Workflow"

The chatbot should identify the intent as a Sales Order workflow query.

It should display:

**Sales Order Workflow**

A brief explanation of the Sales Order process.

Then provide:

1. What is a Sales Order?
2. Why is it required?
3. What are the prerequisites?
4. How does the complete process work?
5. What are the important transaction rules?
6. What are the different stages?
7. What happens after completing each stage?

It should also display the actual Sales Order workflow diagram.

Below the explanation, provide relevant navigation actions:

- View Sales Order Workflow
- Open Sales Order Screen
- View Step-by-Step Guide

Each action must open the correct application page or workflow.

### Example 2: User asks "I want to create a Sales Order"

The chatbot should understand that the user wants to perform an operation, not merely learn about the concept.

Its response should contain:

- A brief explanation of the operation.
- Required prerequisites.
- A visual step-by-step guide with actual screenshots.
- Important validations and transaction rules.
- A direct action such as **Open Sales Order Creation**.

When the user clicks the action, the application should navigate directly to the actual Sales Order creation page.

The user should not have to search through the menus again.

### Example 3: User asks "Where can I configure workflow?"

The chatbot should identify the relevant configuration module.

Its response should explain:
- What the configuration is used for.
- How it affects the business process.
- Where it is configured.
- Which settings and permissions are required.

Then provide a direct link to the actual configuration page, subject to the user's permissions.

### Direct Navigation Requirements

Implement a central Screen and Workflow Registry.

Maintain structured mappings such as:

- Workflow ID.
- Workflow name.
- Module name.
- Screen name.
- Application route.
- Related documentation.
- Workflow diagram location.
- Screenshot references.
- Required permission.
- Navigation metadata.

The chatbot must retrieve actual routes from this registry.

When a user clicks a chatbot navigation link:

1. Validate that the destination is registered.
2. Check whether the user is authenticated.
3. Check whether the user has access to the destination.
4. Navigate directly to the relevant Angular route.
5. Preserve the appropriate application state where necessary.
6. Open the exact intended screen, not just the module landing page.

Use Angular Router or the existing navigation architecture.

Do not generate arbitrary routes using AI-generated strings.

For external HTML pages or prototypes, support registered, verified external URLs as well.

When direct access is not permitted, explain the permission restriction instead of bypassing it.

**The chatbot must work as an intelligent navigation assistant that takes users directly to the functionality they are looking for.**

## 7. Intelligent Query Classification

Implement an intent-classification and retrieval mechanism.

The chatbot should distinguish between:

| User intent | Expected chatbot behaviour |
|---|---|
| General question | Provide a conversational answer |
| ERP concept | Explain the concept using WFX knowledge |
| Workflow search | Show workflow diagram and explanation |
| How-to query | Show screenshot-based step-by-step guide |
| Screen search | Show direct application navigation link |
| Transaction execution | Explain prerequisites and guide the user to the relevant screen |
| Prototype search | Show prototype link and visual demonstration |
| Follow-up query | Continue using previous conversation context |

For example, when the user types "Sales Order", do not immediately return a generic definition.

Identify whether they are looking for:
- Sales Order concept.
- Sales Order workflow.
- Sales Order creation.
- Sales Order modification.
- Sales Order listing.
- Sales Order reports.

Present relevant options or ask a short clarification question when necessary.

## 8. Workflow Diagrams and Visual Explanations

Workflow visualisation must be a first-class feature.

Do not return basic, repetitive or generic flowcharts.

For every available workflow, display the actual business process with:

- Start and end nodes.
- Process steps.
- Decision nodes.
- Conditional branches.
- Alternate paths.
- Approval stages.
- Validation points.
- Connections and directional arrows.
- Clearly labelled transitions.

The diagram must reflect actual WFX business rules.

Provide a readable and interactive workflow visualisation.

Users should be able to zoom, pan, and select individual steps.

When a user selects a step, show its explanation, relevant screenshot, business rules, and related screen navigation.

The workflow diagram and the textual explanation must remain synchronised.

## 9. Chatbot Database and API Architecture

Develop actual backend APIs and database integration.

First inspect the existing backend and database and reuse them.

Create the required data models.

#### ChatConversation
- id
- userId
- title
- createdAt
- updatedAt

#### ChatMessage
- id
- conversationId
- role
- content
- status
- createdAt
- tokenUsage

#### ERPKnowledge
- id
- title
- module
- category
- content
- keywords
- relatedScreenIds
- relatedWorkflowIds
- sourceReference
- updatedAt

#### ERPWorkflow
- id
- workflowName
- module
- description
- workflowDefinition
- diagramReference
- relatedScreenIds
- prerequisites
- businessRules
- updatedAt

#### ERPScreenRegistry
- id
- screenName
- module
- applicationRoute
- description
- screenshotReferences
- requiredPermissions
- relatedWorkflowIds

#### VisualGuide
- id
- title
- relatedScreenId
- relatedWorkflowId
- steps
- screenshotReference
- annotations
- expectedResults

Adapt these entities to the existing database technology and naming conventions.

Do not introduce unnecessary duplicate records.

Support proper indexes, relationships, access control and migrations.

### Backend APIs

Implement endpoints equivalent to:

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/chat/conversations | Create conversation |
| GET | /api/chat/conversations | Get chat history |
| GET | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Get conversation |
| POST | /api/chat/conversations/:id/messages | Send message |
| PATCH | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Rename conversation |
| DELETE | /api/chat/conversations/:id | Delete conversation |
| POST | /api/chat/search | Search ERP knowledge |
| GET | /api/chat/workflows/:id | Retrieve workflow |
| GET | /api/chat/screens/:id | Retrieve screen information |
| GET | /api/chat/guides/:id | Retrieve visual walkthrough |
| GET | /api/chat/navigation/:id | Resolve registered navigation destination |

Implement proper validation, authentication, error handling and response structures.

## 10. AI Model and Knowledge Retrieval

Integrate an actual AI model through the backend.

Reuse any existing AI provider in the project. Otherwise, implement a provider-independent service layer using an official LLM API.

API keys must remain in backend environment variables.

The response-generation pipeline should work as follows:

1. Receive the user's question.
2. Identify the user's intent.
3. Retrieve relevant ERP knowledge.
4. Retrieve related workflow information.
5. Retrieve related screens and routes.
6. Retrieve screenshots and visual guides where applicable.
7. Check user permissions for navigation actions.
8. Generate a context-aware response.
9. Return the answer with structured visual content and relevant action links.
10. Store the conversation and response in the database.

Use structured AI responses so the frontend can distinguish between ordinary text, workflow diagrams, screenshots, step-by-step guides, and navigation actions.

Do not rely on free-form AI text alone to generate navigation links.

The application must be able to render these response types as appropriate.

## 11. Chatbot UI/UX Requirements

Design a modern, premium AI assistant interface consistent with the existing application.

Include:

- Chat history sidebar.
- New conversation button.
- Search previous conversations.
- Main conversation area.
- Suggested questions.
- Message input.
- Typing indicator.
- Stop generation.
- Copy response.
- Regenerate response.
- Relevant workflow cards.
- Screenshot-based guide cards.
- Direct navigation actions.
- Expandable workflow diagrams.
- Responsive mobile layout.

Responses should be visually structured.

For a complex operation, prefer a visual walkthrough with screenshots over several long paragraphs.

Keep the most relevant actions visible and easy to access.

The chatbot should feel like a knowledgeable product expert, not a generic customer support chatbot.

## 12. Testing Scenarios and Acceptance Criteria

Test the complete implementation with real API calls and actual stored data.

**Scenario A: General question**

User: "Explain APIs."

Expected: An intelligent response with examples.

**Scenario B: Workflow query**

User: "Show me the Sales Order workflow."

Expected:
- Relevant explanation.
- Actual workflow diagram.
- Step descriptions.
- Related screens.
- Direct workflow navigation.

**Scenario C: Operational query**

User: "How do I create a Sales Order?"

Expected:
- Prerequisites.
- Actual screenshots.
- Numbered click instructions.
- Expected results at each step.
- Direct Open Sales Order action.

**Scenario D: Trims Scan query**

User: "Explain the complete trims outward process."

Expected:
- Reference to the running Trims Scan prototype.
- Relevant screenshots.
- GRN, Pick List, GDN, Location, Print Doc and Outward Note steps.
- Actual step-by-step explanations.
- Direct prototype link.

**Scenario E: Direct screen navigation**

User: "Open the Sales Order screen."

Expected:
- Resolve the correct registered route.
- Check permissions.
- Navigate directly to the Sales Order screen.
- Do not redirect to the home page or module landing page.

**Scenario F: Unknown information**

User asks about a workflow that does not exist in the knowledge base.

Expected:
- Clearly state that verified information is unavailable.
- Do not invent business rules, routes, screenshots, or workflow steps.

**Scenario G: Persistence**

- Create a conversation.
- Ask multiple questions.
- Refresh the application.
- Reopen the conversation.
- Verify that the entire history is restored.

Also test mobile responsiveness, API failures, authorization, performance and existing application functionality.

## 13. Mandatory Implementation Rules

- Do not deliver just a chatbot UI.
- Do not deliver only architecture or code snippets.
- Do not use static responses as actual AI functionality.
- Do not use fake screenshots.
- Do not generate imaginary WFX business rules.
- Do not generate unregistered navigation links.
- Do not leave backend APIs as placeholders.
- Do not simulate database persistence using static arrays.
- Do not hardcode API credentials.
- Do not bypass permissions.
- Do not break existing application functionality.
- Do not make all chatbot responses lengthy text.
- Prioritise visual explanations and meaningful actions.
- Reuse existing components and architecture.
- Test each feature before marking it complete.

If screenshots, documentation, API credentials, routes or other required information are missing, identify the dependency clearly and implement everything that can be completed without inventing information.

## 14. Final Deliverables

After implementation, provide:

1. Working AI chatbot.
2. Backend APIs and their documentation.
3. Database schema and migrations.
4. AI provider integration.
5. WFX ERP knowledge-base implementation.
6. Intent classification and retrieval mechanism.
7. Screen and workflow registry.
8. Screenshot-based visual guidance system.
9. Workflow diagrams and interactive explanations.
10. Direct application navigation integration.
11. Responsive UI implementation.
12. Test results and known limitations.
13. Environment configuration and deployment instructions.

## FINAL PRODUCT VISION

I want users to interact with the application naturally.

They should be able to type:

"How does the Sales Order process work?"

The chatbot should understand the question, explain the business process, display an actual workflow diagram, show each step visually with screenshots, explain what the user needs to click, show the expected result, and provide a direct link to the Sales Order screen.

Similarly, when a user asks:

"How do I process trims outward?"

The chatbot should display the complete Trims Scan process with actual prototype screenshots, clear visual directions, and a link to open the prototype.

The user should never have to manually search through multiple menus, browse lengthy documentation, or guess which screen to open.

**Think of this as an AI-powered WFX ERP Product Expert + Process Trainer + Workflow Navigator combined into one intelligent assistant.**

The ultimate goal is to make the ERP application easier to learn, easier to navigate, and easier to operate — even for a completely new user.

Build this as a production-oriented, fully functional application feature, not a visual demonstration.

**What the chatbot does now:**
- **Trims Scan:** I captured all 49 screens of the six prototype flows (GRN, Pick List, GDN, Location, Print Doc, Outward Note). 28 of the 49 steps have a marker exactly where to tap; the rest show the screen without a marker (typed-value and camera steps, and each flow's final step). I've created the file the key goes into, `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\.env`, with an empty spot for the key. I can't create or paste API keys for you, so you need to get the key and paste it in yourself.

**1. Get a key** (needs an Anthropic Console account with billing set up)
- Open **https://console.anthropic.com/** in your browser and sign in, or create an account. Your company may already have one, so ask your IT or admin team first.
- Go to **Settings → API Keys → Create Key** and give it a name, for example "WFX Knowledge Hub".
- Copy the key now; it's shown only once and starts with `sk-ant-`.
- Make sure **Settings → Billing** has credit or a payment method, otherwise calls are refused. You can set a monthly spend limit there.

**2. Put the key in the file**
- Open `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\.env` in Notepad:

```powershell
notepad "D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\.env"
```

- Paste the key right after `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=`, with no spaces or quotes, so the line reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…`, then save.
- Don't share this file or the key in chat.

**3. Restart the server**
- Click the server's terminal tab and press **Ctrl+C**, then run:

```powershell
cd "D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN"; .\start-on-network.ps1
```

- The log should show a line saying "settings read from .env".

**4. Switch Claude on in the app**
- Sign in at http://127.0.0.1:8787/, open **Knowledge → Admin**, and scroll to **AI provider**.
- Tick "The organisation allows sending WFX knowledge passages to the AI provider", set **Provider: Claude**, write who approved it, and click **Save**.
- The top of that section should then say "Key configured on the server: claude · Active: yes".

**5. Try it**
- In the Assistant, type "hi", then a WFX question, then "open the GRN screen".

Claude Opus 5.5 is used by default, at about $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens; a typical chat message costs a few cents. To use a cheaper model, add a second line `AI_CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5` to `.env` and restart.

I went through the questions people actually typed into your live assistant and re-asked each one. Several were being misunderstood, mainly because Claude isn't switched on yet, so the built-in keyword matcher was answering. I fixed the ones that were misread; they now answer correctly on your D: server, and all tests pass.

| Question asked | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "If my consumption is 1 Meter and my loss is 10%, Shrinkage is 5%, Wastage is 2% then tell me the total consumption" | Showed an unrelated spreadsheet | Runs the consumption calculation: **1.192982**, with each step shown |
| "if i have my consumption of 1 Meter and loss is 10%, WASTAGE IS 2%…" | Showed the same spreadsheet | **1.133333**, with each step shown |
| "when i dont select purchase officer and user group then what happens" | Answered about a different topic | Indents come in Inactive status by default and must be marked Active by hand |
| "i have my indent marked as inactive, why is it so." / "when is indent marked as inactive" | Answered about OC closure | The same Inactive-indent rule (fixed by this morning's rule rewrite) |
| "loss %" | "Not documented" | Shows the definition of Loss % |

What changed in how questions are read:
- **Numbers in a sentence:** two or more numbers plus "tell me", "total", "what is" or "how much" now count as a calculation request.
- **Everyday words:** "consumption" fills "Cons Qty", and "1 meter" or "500 pcs" is read as just the number.
- **Negations:** "don't", "didn't" and "doesn't" count as negations, and "select" or "choose" means the same as "set" or "fill".
- **The % sign:** a % on its own no longer breaks the search, so "loss %" means Loss %.

These six questions are now in the evaluation set so they can't quietly break again. The evaluation scores 39/39 on finding the right source and 0 of 14 on hallucination checks, and all 112 tests pass.

Two of the questions people asked still aren't answered fully:
- **"how to cancel indent from mrp":** no cancellation procedure is stored, so it says it is only partly documented.
- **"Generate workflow for costing to FPPO":** it asks which workflow you mean.

Once the Claude key is in `D:\WFX Knowledge hub\ASN\.env` and you approve Claude under Admin › AI provider, Claude will interpret every question in plain language. These fixes keep the assistant sensible when Claude is off or unavailable.
